description: Excel formulas preserved in an xlsx export from the Svelte 5 data grid. A Q3 budget has three computed columns, Subtotal, Tax and Total, plus a SUM footer; the export builds a real OOXML workbook in the browser with JSZip and writes those cells as formula elements such as B2*$D$1, not cached numbers, so Excel recomputes when a quantity is edited. Numbers and inline strings share the sheet without a shared-strings part; @svgrid/enterprise offers the same through the formulas option of exportData.

faq.question: How is a formula written into the xlsx?
faq.answer: As a cell element with an f child holding the formula text, for example B2*$D$1, and no cached value. Excel evaluates it on open, so the sheet is live rather than a snapshot.

faq.question: Why build the workbook by hand?
faq.answer: To show that an xlsx is a zip of XML parts and that formulas, numbers and inline strings can be emitted directly. The enterprise exporter does the same with formulas: true so every grid in the app shares one code path.

faq.question: Do relative and absolute references both work?
faq.answer: Yes. Row-relative references such as B2 are generated per row and absolute references such as $D$1 point at the tax rate cell, exactly as typed in Excel.
